chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to him, “How does the junub perform ghusl?” He said: “If no semen has touched his palm, he dips it into the water, then begins with his private part and cleans it, then pours three handfuls over his head, then pours over his right shoulder twice and over his left shoulder twice. So whatever the water flows over, it has sufficed him.”

And all of these reports indicate the obligation of sequence in ghusl, because when he connected the ruling of some limbs to others with ‘then,’ and there is no disagreement that it indicates sequence, this further increases the sense of obligation as well.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him; it fulfilled the required washing
key_terms.بِفَرْجِهِ: with his private part; the area to be cleaned first
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ أَكُفٍّ: three handfuls of water poured over the head
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen, whose contact affects the washing procedure mentioned here
key_terms.مَنْكِبِهِ: his shoulder, referring to the right and left sides in washing
key_terms.ٱلتَّرْتِيبِ: the required sequence or order in performing ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: How should a junub perform ghusl, and is sequence obligatory in it?
ai.summary: This report explains the manner of performing ghusl for janabah, beginning with cleaning the private part and then washing the head, right side, and left side in sequence. The accompanying statement emphasizes that these reports establish the obligation of order in ghusl, based on the wording of sequential action.
